drugRefs.why: Ceftriaxone is first-line in regions with high rates of multidrug-resistant and fluoroquinolone-resistant S. Typhi, providing reliable activity and good clinical response.

drugRefs.coverage: Effective oral option for uncomplicated enteric fever, particularly useful where oral step-down or outpatient management is appropriate.
Should only be used where local susceptibility data confirm fluoroquinolone-susceptible Salmonella — resistance is widespread in many endemic areas including South Asia.

coverageMatrix.completeness: Ceftriaxone or azithromycin reliably covers the expected pathogen given regional resistance patterns.
gaps: Ciprofloxacin should not be used empirically without local susceptibility confirmation due to widespread fluoroquinolone resistance.

stewardship.deescalation: If blood culture confirms fluoroquinolone-susceptible S. Typhi, can switch to oral ciprofloxacin for outpatient completion. If azithromycin-susceptible and clinically improving, complete oral course without escalation to IV ceftriaxone.

drugs.why: Ceftriaxone is first-line in regions with high rates of multidrug-resistant and fluoroquinolone-resistant S. Typhi, providing reliable activity and good clinical response.

drugs.coverage: Effective oral option for uncomplicated enteric fever, particularly useful where oral step-down or outpatient management is appropriate.
Should only be used where local susceptibility data confirm fluoroquinolone-susceptible Salmonella — resistance is widespread in many endemic areas including South Asia.

framework: Empiric fluoroquinolones should be avoided in enteric fever in regions with known high resistance (including most of South Asia) — ceftriaxone or azithromycin is preferred.
Confirm diagnosis with blood culture; Widal test alone is unreliable and should not be the sole basis for diagnosis or prolonged treatment.
Treat for the full recommended duration to reduce relapse and chronic carriage risk.
